reasoning: For a right triangle inscribed in a circle, the hypotenuse is the diameter of the circle. The 3-4-5 triangle has a hypotenuse of 5, so the radius of circle Q is 5/2. The area of circle Q is π*(5/2)² = 25π/4. The 5-12-13 triangle has a hypotenuse of 13, so the radius of circle A is 13/2. The area of circle A is π*(13/2)² = 169π/4. The ratio of the areas is (25π/4)/(169π/4) = 25/169.
